pageCache.text:
What success means to us
Small Independent School of the Year
“Hard to put into words, the magic of St Mary’s is in my daughter’s ebullience and confidence.”
“Teachers balance academic rigour with creative learning.”
“When drop-offs are as cheerful as pick-ups, you know you have picked the right school.”
Top 5 UK Prep School
88% rate pupil wellbeing and happiness as good or excellent; 89% rate teaching and learning as good or excellent.
“From a shy introverted 3-year-old, to an articulate, smiling and confident almost nine-year-old… that’s the magic of St Mary’s.”
11+ Results 2026: 100 offers, 29 scholarships & an average of 3.6 offers per pupil!
‘Highly Commended’ for Outstanding School Sport
“Pupils… care for one another and are proud of their school.”
Admissions
Enter your child’s date of birth
Space to Explore
Front courtyard
You’ll find St. Mary’s on the beautiful tree-lined Fitzjohn’s Avenue, linking Hampstead with Swiss Cottage. Our courtyard serves as the main entrance to our school. Don’t let the grand yet unassuming Victorian building pass you by; you’ll discover five floors of inspiring and spacious learning spaces inside, two halls, a Chapel, a virtual reality room, and five playgrounds!
Photo Gallery
Entrance Hall
Our breathtaking entrance hall upholds many of the original features of this nineteenth-century home. Every day you will see our stunningly preserved floor mosaic, grade-listed oak panelling, and our majestic blue staircase. We hope our entrance hall mirrors the warm and welcoming experience of our school.
Photo Gallery
Library
Once a nineteenth-century billiard and games room, our modern library is now home to over 1,000 books. All children have the opportunity to visit during the week and take home a variety of new and classic books. You can also choose a book and enjoy reading in one of our cosy reading chairs. It’s a place where imagination and creativity can run wild!
Photo Gallery
Chapel
The spiritual and physical heart of St. Mary’s, our Chapel has been in situ since 1939. It’s a beautiful and tranquil place, open to all members of the school community. It is used daily, from Mass to assemblies, choir rehearsals to concerts. We have a part-time Chaplain to lead our services and times of reflection, and who offers pastoral support to those in need. All are welcome to visit our lovely Chapel.
Photo Gallery
Chapel Hall
Underneath our Chapel is the Chapel Hall, one of our two school halls. Today it is predominantly used for gymnastics and other sports, when weather prevents us from being outside. The Chapel Hall is also home to our Year 6 production each summer, and a variety of internal and parent events. These include our annual Inter-house competitions, the PTA Quiz, Christmas Fair, Art Fair and Charity Breakfasts, to name a few.
Photo Gallery
Mary Ward Hall
Opening over a decade ago, the Mary Ward Hall is our latest extension. It is fitted with a moveable wall, enabling multiple events to take place at once. On a day-to-day basis it is home to our Music & Drama department, but is also used for our weekly assemblies and many of the over 40 clubs taking place at St. Mary’s each week. The MWH has a stage, smaller than that in our Chapel Hall, for our annual Nativities and Prize Giving ceremonies.
Photo Gallery
Playground
St. Mary’s is lucky to have impressive outdoor spaces for a school in central London. There is much to explore. We have a fishpond, pirate ship climbing frame, a rooftop playground, a bike garden, a climbing wall, a peace garden, and a Secret Garden for EYFS pupils. We aim to be outside as much as possible during the day, and strongly advocate the benefits of fresh air and play for our girls’ physical and mental wellbeing.
Photo Gallery
Blue Playground
Our blue playground serves as an all-weather, full-size Netball court. It is used for a variety of sports, both within the curriculum and as part of our extensive extra-curricular club programme. Girls in Upper School will also often play fixtures against other schools on our blue playground; parents are welcome to come and watch. We certainly have much to celebrate, with national finalists in Netball, Football and Gymnastics this year alone.
Photo Gallery
Classroom
Throughout our spacious five floors you will find many inspiring classrooms. All have been refurbished in recent years, blending perfectly our traditional education with modern, pro-technology learning. Girls will spend most mornings with their class teacher in their own classroom, for form time and key subject learning. Lessons for the remainder of the day are dedicated to specialist teaching at sites throughout the school, including Science, Music, Art, PE and French.
Photo Gallery
Global Learning Centre
At the top of St. Mary’s, you will find our unique, pioneering Global Learning Centre. We consider ourselves champions for girls’ education and STEAM subjects. Within our GLC you will find our Science room, an Engineering & Robotics Lab (complete with Lego robots and 3D printers), a video green screen, our green room, and the highlight of any school tour, our ‘Launch Pad’ virtual reality room. We have headsets for all children to explore the world around them. Older pupils will be given a laptop or iPad during their learning in the GLC, to become proficient in a range of technologies and become leaders of tomorrow.

Welcome to St Mary’s School, Hampstead
An independent Catholic Prep School in Hampstead, North London educating girls from 2 ½ to 11 years and boys from 2 ½ to 4 years.
Welcome to St. Mary’s School, Hampstead, a top choice among Prep schools in London. At St. Mary’s, we embrace the diverse talents and unique contributions each pupil brings to our vibrant, inclusive community.
Our philosophy is rooted in fostering strong partnerships between home, school, parish, and the broader Hampstead community. We stand out among schools in London for delivering exceptional education in a secure, supportive, and innovative environment. Our emphasis on holistic development ensures that every child flourishes academically, socially, and morally.
We warmly invite you to schedule a tour or join us at our next Open Morning to experience the St. Mary’s difference first-hand. As a leading Prep school in North London, we offer a dynamic and enriching curriculum designed to engage and challenge, nurturing a lifelong love of learning. Our dedicated teachers employ innovative teaching methods, focusing on critical thinking and creativity to equip our pupils with the skills they need for future success.
In addition to academic excellence, St. Mary’s provides a well-rounded education with ample opportunities for girls to explore their interests in arts, music, sports, and extracurricular activities. We cherish the individuality of each pupil, supporting them to reach their full potential and preparing them to become compassionate and responsible members of society.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headmistress | St Mary's Girls School Hampstead
pageCache.text:
I am delighted to welcome you to St Mary’s School, Hampstead, a school that provides a sense of belonging to each and every girl from Pre-Nursery through to Year 6, as well as boys in Pre-Nursery and Nursery. We pride ourselves on our family-feel and the sense of community and ethos that are so tangible as soon as you walk through the front door. Every individual is valued and known, allowing the children in our care to develop and flourish. We firmly believe that a happy child will naturally become a successful child and we therefore take academic rigour and our varied curriculum as seriously as we do our pastoral care.
We aim to instil four key qualities in our pupils: we encourage the children to be risk-takers in their learning, their play and their extra-curricular pursuits. We teach them to be resilient, not to fall at the first hurdle, to “fail” well and to understand that it is from their mistakes that they will learn best. Pupils at St Mary’s are respectful of each other but also of themselves, underpinned by a strong sense of value and worth of every individual. Finally, we ask them to be reflective on their faith, their behaviour and their academic work.
We are a school proud of our Catholic heritage spanning over more than 150 years. Part of our ethos is to welcome families of all faiths and none; everyone has a place here. Our St Mary’s Way is the spirit by which we live: to treat other people as you would like to be treated, to do your best to be your best, to be honest and truthful, to listen to each other, to be kind and helpful, to forgive, and to share.
Unashamedly an all-girls’ school, with boys welcome in our Pre-Nursery and Nursery too, I see the benefits of such a setting every day as the calm and focused environment allows the girls to be themselves, to take risks, and to think big. As our pioneering founder, Mary Ward, wisely said, “There is no such difference between men and women that women may not do great things.”
We strive to provide a forward-thinking, innovative and outstanding Prep education for girls, and will always invest in our pupils, staff and lovely facilities. You can read our current ‘Vision & Future 2026-2029’ document here.
Please do contact our Head of Marketing, Admissions & Development if you would like to come and visit our exceptional school – you will be made most welcome. I very much look forward to meeting you and your daughter.
Charlotte Owen Headmistress

Our Chaplaincy
The Chaplaincy sits at the heart of spiritual life at St Mary’s. It provides relevant spiritual and pastoral support to all students, parents, and staff, embracing our Catholic identity and drawing inspiration from our Foundress, Mary Ward. The Chaplaincy welcomes and serves the whole school community, including those who are:
Practising Catholics
From other Christian denominations
From other faith backgrounds or none
Our Mission
Collective Worship & Liturgy
Each student participates in a three-weekly cycle of Mass, Gospel Service, and Exposition of the Blessed Sacrament from Years 1-6. Feast of the Immaculate Conception (December 8th)
Mary Ward Day (January 24th)

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education at St Mary's School, Hampstead | Catholic School
pageCache.text:
At the heart of our curriculum is the belief that religious growth is central to each child’s development. We aim to nurture religiously literate, engaged individuals who reflect spiritually and think ethically, applying their faith in daily life.
Our Aims
Teaching R.E. Focuses On
Reflecting on personal and others’ experiences.
Developing an honest, open, and reflective attitude.
Promoting respect, friendship, and goodwill.
Approach
Equal Opportunities & Inclusion
We provide an inclusive environment where all children are valued and supported in their religious education, regardless of ability, race, gender, or background.
Prayer & Worship
Prayer and liturgical practices, such as Mass and Exposition of the Blessed Sacrament, are integral to school life. Weekly services and prayer sessions foster a strong sense of community and faith.
Curriculum Time
We dedicate 10% of the timetable to R.E., with 2 hours and 15 minutes in Key Stage 1, and 2 hours and 30 minutes in Key Stage 2. Early Years follow the Diocesan “Come and See” framework, aligned with the EYFS curriculum.
Supporting Growth
Through play, exploration, and critical thinking, our children develop both academically and spiritually, preparing them to become thoughtful, compassionate individuals within the school community and beyond.
Planning
Teachers use the Come and See online resources to plan lessons, ensuring differentiation by task or outcome to meet all students’ needs. Spiritual opportunities are incorporated into lesson plans.
Other Faiths
We teach about other faiths as part of the Come and See programme, with specific focus on Hinduism, Judaism, and Islam throughout the year. Visitors from other faiths and educational visits enhance this learning.
Links Between R.E. and Other Subjects
R.E. connects with subjects like Drama, Art, Music, ICT, and PSHCEE. We use a variety of strategies to adapt learning to students’ needs.
Growth (PSHCEE)
In Growth lessons, children explore moral choices using the Ten:Ten scheme, and the values of the Gospels through the St. Mary’s Way and the school’s ethos. The RSE policy guides this area.
ICT in R.E.
ICT supports R.E. learning through interactive whiteboards, iPads, Chromebooks, and audio-visual tools like the Global Learning Centre.
Resources
Teachers have access to planning, RECD, assessment grids, prayers, liturgical calendar events, and various R.E. resources in the school’s R.E. Resource Room.
Assessment
Assessment follows Diocesan guidelines, with continuous teacher evaluations and tracking of pupil progress. In EYFS, assessments are based on observations and recorded in a class book.
Monitoring
R.E. teaching is monitored through lesson observations, planning reviews, work scrutiny, and regular contact with the Diocese.
CPD (Continuing Professional Development)
Teachers receive R.E. training, both school-based and from the Diocese. CPD needs are identified through performance management.
Management of R.E.
The Leaders of Learning for R.E. are responsible for improving teaching quality, supporting staff, ensuring adherence to the RECD and upcoming Religious Education Directory, managing assessment and resources, and facilitating professional development. They also oversee prayer and worship activities and work with the Diocesan R.E. advisor.
The Headteacher ensures R.E. is a key focus in the school, monitors teaching and learning, and supports the Catholic ethos of the school. Please find our RE Policy here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Ethos at St Mary's Girls School Hampstead
pageCache.text:
St Mary’s School provides a holistic education where excellent academic provision, rigour and results complement our outstanding pastoral care; children are nurtured in a caring community in which their happiness is paramount so that they can achieve their full potential both academically and as a responsible citizen with moral integrity.
As a staff body, we are committed to delivering the best teaching practice possible for the children in our care so that the breadth of the curriculum is wide, and girls are rigorously prepared for excellent senior school destinations. Preparatory school is exactly that – the preparation of the essential foundations of all that the girls will learn and continue to learn throughout their school and university careers. We place emphasis on STEAM and this can be seen in our Global Learning Centre; the space includes a cutting-edge Engineering and Robotics Lab, Virtual Reality Launch Pad, Art and Design Studio as well as a Green Room. We balance this focus on technology with an emphasis on creative and physical development. Music, drama, art and sports are an essential part of school life and involve everyone. Pupils also benefit from our extensive and leafy outdoor space.
Alongside our excellence in academics, we pride ourselves on our outstanding pastoral care. This is due to the warm, nurturing feel of our community where each child is known and valued. This provides a sense of belonging and value for the individual so that they feel recognised and genuinely cared for. St Mary’s upholds strong moral and spiritual principles, proudly recognising our Catholic values, but it is also an inclusive environment in which many other faiths are represented and celebrated. We aspire to educate girls to become confident, resilient and caring leaders of the future.
At St Mary’s, we celebrate our Catholic values, which include kindness, compassion, tolerance, care, honesty, integrity, forgiveness and justice. Our St Mary’s Way is something that is emphasised by all so that girls know how to conduct themselves not just while at school but also in the wider community. We also welcome into school those of other faiths and cultures to present workshops on the similarities, not just the differences, of their faith compared to Christianity, to promote unity, respect and tolerance.
We endeavour to promote the common good and support those who are less fortunate than ourselves, remembering that every human being is of equal value, whatever their circumstances. To that end, we fundraise for one school charity each year, chosen by parents, pupils, and staff, and we will fundraise regularly for other charitable events throughout the year, such as October’s Harvest Festival and November’s Poppy Appeal. We consider that giving time to charity is equally as important as giving money and resources. Lenten Promises have included making care packages for the homeless and picking up litter in the local area. These small acts of charity all help to build compassion, respect, resilience, understanding, care and responsibility for the wider world.
We welcome parents to become involved in the life of our school through our Friends of St Mary’s and we encourage parents to role model our values at home as best they can so that both home and school are able to support the girls to become the best version of themselves.
We also have a commitment in our School Development Plan to sustainability; our installation of LED lighting and solar panels are some of our initiatives to try and reduce our carbon footprint and care for the world around us.
As a charity, we are a non-profit organisation which means that any profit made goes back into the education of our pupils in terms of facilities and resources. We also use such money to help fund bursaries of up to 100% and warmly welcome applications from families who may need some assistance with school fees.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spiritual Life at St Mary's Girls School Hampstead | Catholic School
pageCache.text:
At St Mary’s School, we follow the ‘Ten Ten’ programme for Religious Education. We work on common themes throughout the school. As a result, the children experience a programme which enables and supports their faith development and spiritual life.
All children participate in a variety of acts of worship, such as Assemblies, Mass, Gospel Services and Praying Together activities. The school also celebrates the Holy Days of Obligation together.
Father Chris Connor is the School Chaplain. He guides us spiritually in our everyday work and provides wonderful pastoral support and care for the whole school community. All of our Masses and liturgies take place in our own school chapel, which are led by Fr Chris.
Children are prepared for the Sacraments of First Holy Communion and Confession with the close involvement of parents and staff. Pupils are encouraged to be compassionate to others and to live out the Gospel values of loving one another by involving themselves in charitable work in the local community and supporting various charities around the world.
Mass
We celebrate Mass in our beautiful chapel at least once every half-term. The Chapel is the spiritual heart of our school It is also where we hold any religious services as well as our weekly Praying Together Services. Whole school Masses are celebrated at the start and end of the term and on Holy Days. Children, staff and parents use the chapel at many other times during the school day; it is a wonderful resource and all are welcome there.
Chapel Choir
The Year 6 girls form the beautiful Chapel Choir. They sing regularly at Masses and other occasions, such as our annual Carol Concert and celebrations at school. The Chapel Choir hand over their robes to the Year 5s at their Leavers’ Mass which is always a poignant but joyful event.

pageCache.pageTitle: FAQS | Trustees & Governors | St Mary's Girls School Hampstead
pageCache.text:
Who owns St Mary’s School?
St Mary’s School was founded in 1926 by the Institute of the Blessed Virgin Mary (now known as the Congregation of Jesus). In 1992 a group of parents and others set up a new registered charity to take over the running of the School in order to save it from closure. St Mary’s School is a company limited by guarantee and the trustees of the charity are also the directors of the company. The school buildings are owned by St Mary’s School.
What do the trustees do?
St Mary’s School has a two tier structure of governance. The trustees are responsible for maintaining the objects of the charity, its administration and finances, risk assessment and overall strategy, as well as ensuring that the School complies with company law. The trustees appoint the head. There are five trustees. They meet three times a year and attend the AGM.
What do the governors do?
The governors are responsible for the general direction, policies and priorities of the School within the budgets and objectives established by the trustees. They offer support and guidance to the Headmistress, but also hold the School to account for the quality of education it provides and the standards it achieves. The governors ensure the safety of the school environment and review the effectiveness of our child protection policies. Some governors are also trustees. There are currently 9 governors.
Are the trustees and governors paid?
No. Trustees and governors give their time and expertise voluntarily for the benefit of the School. Most have had children at the school or have been on the teaching staff. The rewards are to be found in the many successes and achievements of the School. All governors attend training courses and spend time keeping up to date with developments in school governance.
What happens to the profits made by the School?
The School does not make a profit in the way that commercial companies do. Any surplus after bills have been paid is made to work for the benefit of the School and ploughed back into purposes which support our primary charitable purpose – to promote and advance Roman Catholic education and the Roman Catholic religion in particular. The School is committed to supporting pupils who for financial reasons may not have access to independent preparatory school education founded on the Catholic faith. We employ some of our annual surplus in providing bursaries based on financial means testing. Further information, including copies of the trustees’ annual report and accounts, are available on the Charity Commission’s website.
How often do the governors meet?
The governing body meets in full session once a term and the main sub-committees, Education and Staffing, Finance and General Purposes and Health and Safety, meet at least once a term and report to the meetings of the governing body.
How does the Trust set the fees?
The Trust has regard to the level of fees that are appropriate for the education provided and the ability of parents to pay them. Fees are set at a level which will generate a fund out of which we can pay for the School’s staff, facilities and resources and also provide bursaries to families who could not otherwise afford to pay the fees and public benefit to members of the wider community, in accordance with the objects of the School.
How does the Trust ensure that the School recruits and retains high quality staff?
All teachers applying for posts are observed delivering lessons and interacting with the children and staff team. They then take part in a full interview, with a panel consisting of present staff, governors and the Senior Leadership Team. Once offered a post at the school, organised induction is delivered over a period of weeks. The management structure ensures that there are many opportunities for progression and promotion within the school. Staff participate in high quality external professional development courses and in-house training.
What vision do the governors and trustees have for the future of the School?
The School’s vision is set out in our Mission Statement. The governors seek to ensure that our aims and values are fulfilled through the strategic plan agreed by the trustees and the head and implemented in the three-year School Development Plan. The Plan for 2026-2029 identifies the current needs and priorities for each area of curriculum and management in detail and helps translate long-term vision into short-term achievable goals.
How can I become a governor?
The governing body plays an important part in the life of the School and so we plan ahead by identifying individuals with relevant skills who might be willing to replace governors as they retire. We aim to have a good spread of talents and experience represented on the governing body so that we can continue to be as effective as possible in developing the School and providing support and challenge to the senior leadership team. Parents and former parents will have a thorough understanding of our School and the values that underpin it and may be well placed to add value to our board. If you are committed to our ethos and would like to help us build our School and plan for the future, then please get in touch so that we can discuss this further, either with Miss Charlotte Owen or with the Chair of Governors, Mr Sean Murphy, by emailing him at Sean.Murphy@stmaryshampstead.org.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: Residential Trips at St Mary's Girls School Hampstead
pageCache.text:
Residential trips begin in Year 4 and encourage the girls to be risk takers, trying new challenges. They also help the girls forge life-long friendships. In Year 6, there is a combined intensive French language and skiing trip to France. This trip combines enrichment, cultural experience and skiing.

pageCache.pageTitle: Private Upper School for Girls aged 9-11 Years | St Mary's Girls School Hampstead
pageCache.text:
In the Upper School at St Mary’s, we follow the National Curriculum and supplement this with the Independent Schools Examination Board curriculum.
Located in the affluent neighbourhood of Hampstead, our school boasts impressive academic results (and senior school destinations) and a diverse range of extracurricular activities. We place great emphasis on empowering young girls to excel both academically and personally. We are able to offer an extremely broad and balanced curriculum focusing on individual strengths and talents. We believe that this broad curriculum allows for great enrichment across the whole school.
Our curriculum provides opportunities for all girls to learn and achieve, promotes their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development and prepares them for the many opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of life.
The Upper School includes girls aged 9 – 11 years and covers Years 4, 5 & 6.

With a strong focus on developing leadership skills and promoting self-confidence, St Mary’s aims to prepare its students for success in all aspects of their lives.

Teachers at this stage emphasise independent learning and responsibility, helping girls develop the study habits and organisational skills necessary for future academic success. The broad and balanced curriculum is complemented by a wide range of extracurricular activities, including music, drama, sports, and modern languages, ensuring that each girl has the opportunity to explore her interests and talents.
In addition to academic rigour, St Mary’s places great importance on personal growth and leadership development. The independent upper school fosters a supportive environment where girls are encouraged to take on new challenges, build confidence, and develop a strong sense of self. Opportunities for leadership are abundant, with roles such as school council representatives, house captains, and peer mentors allowing students to contribute to the school community and develop their leadership skills. The focus on character education, empathy, and resilience helps to prepare the girls not only for the academic demands of senior school but also for the broader challenges of life. By the time girls leave us, girls are well-equipped, both academically and personally, to step confidently into the next phase of their educational journey.

pageCache.text:
Pre-Nursery, Nursery & Reception
St Mary’s warmly welcomes girls from the age of 2 years 6 months into our vibrant and nurturing community. Encompassing Pre-Nursery (age 2 ½-3), Nursery (age 3-4) and Reception (age 4-5), our EYFS department is dedicated to providing the best possible start to your daughter’s educational journey with fully qualified teachers. We also warmly welcome boys from the age of 2 years 6 months to 4 years, in our Pre-Nursery and Nursery.
Housed in a colourful, homely environment, our EYFS boasts a purpose-built STEAM corner and a lovely Secret Garden, fostering creativity and exploration.
Why choose St Mary’s?
Pre-Nursery and Nursery children attend five mornings per week, with the flexible option to extend to a full day. We view every child as an individual, learning at their own pace through focussed and purposeful play.
Our comprehensive curriculum covers seven areas of learning: personal, social and emotional development; communication; physical education; literacy; mathematics; understanding the world; and expressive art and design. St. Mary’s is committed to nurturing well-rounded, confident and curious young learners. More information about the Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum and our 7 areas of learning can be found here.
You can view our EYFS curriculum statement here.
More information about the EYFS can be found here:
We are also proud to have achieved Millie’s Mark in our EYFS department. Millie’s Mark is a voluntary award for early years settings that demonstrates a commitment to going above and beyond the minimum requirements for keeping young children safe. It recognises settings where 100% of staff working directly with children are trained in paediatric first aid, with an emphasis not only on completing the training but on ensuring that staff remain confident, prepared and able to put their knowledge into practice should an emergency arise. This provides reassurance to families that children’s safety is firmly at the heart of our EYFS provision.

Year-Round Provision
From September 2026, St Mary’s is proud to offer year-round nursery provision for children from the age of 2½, providing families in Hampstead and the wider local community with greater flexibility and continuity throughout the year. During term time, children can attend our nurturing Pre-Nursery and Nursery, with additional on-site holiday provision available during the school holidays through our partnership with Let’s Leap, an Ofsted-registered holiday camp provider.
Importantly, the holiday provision is open to all local families – children do not need to be existing pupils at St Mary’s to attend. Current pupils, siblings and children from other nurseries and schools are all warmly welcomed. This means families can benefit from high-quality childcare in a safe, familiar and stimulating environment throughout much of the year, with children able to enjoy a wide range of sports, creative activities, games and adventures while building confidence and making new friends.
To find out more about our holiday provision, including dates, fees and booking information, please visit the St Mary’s Holiday Club page or book directly with Let’s Leap.
